rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Forcing functions stay, scripted reactions go; forcing functions live in prompts, not body prose.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm check: the rule guards against a speed-runner who skips body prose and therefore never encounters the pedagogy-load-bearing move, because it was narrated only in prose instead of enacted in the fence they paste. Read `curriculum/prompts/ae101-prework-one-at-a-time.md` (full file) — the actual mechanism ('Use the AskUserQuestion tool for speeding up screening... One candidate at a time.') is IN the fence, not narrated only in body. Body lines 64-68 ('push back if it dumps all four criteria at once... If Claude's screening feels like everything-at-once, ask Claude to use the AskUserQuestion tool...') only tell the STUDENT when to reach for the fence — this matches the explicit carve-out: 'optional push-backs / refinements... can live in body.' The primary screening move (`{{prompt:ae101-prework-screen-and-ready}}`) is also fenced. Harm (a speed-runner silently missing the forcing function) is not present: the fence carries the mechanism regardless of whether the body sentence was read.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Non-blocking: lines 64 and 68 both narrate the same trigger condition ('dumps all four criteria at once' / 'feels like everything-at-once') — minor redundancy, not a rule-16 violation, but a sentence could be cut without losing the pointer to the fence.

stealing_the_mood: opinionated_senior, phase 7 (bug-screen rehearsal): 7/10 — reads as slightly over-narrated for a persona who'd have pushed back reflexively without the body naming the trigger; fix would frame the recovery prompt as available ('if you want it') rather than prescribed ('push back if').

fast_operator, phase 7 (bug-screen rehearsal): 7/10 — the rehearsal's forcing function is contingent on BOTH the body sentence being read AND Claude dumping all four criteria; on a clean screening run this reader never exercises the push-back move at all, though the visible artifact is identical.

notes: Teaching-moment-lands check (no check_strategy_tie_in rule_index, per the completeness contract): Step 5's push-back rehearsal reliably delivers the SAME visible artifact (a picked bug, confirmed readiness) across all three personas, but the underlying skill practice is fragile for the fast_operator persona — the rehearsal only fires if Claude happens to dump all four candidate criteria at once AND the reader reads the triggering body sentence. Not a REVISE (mood floor is still met at 7, and rule 16's carve-out is satisfied — the mechanism itself lives in the fence), but the artifact can look identical whether or not the skill was actually practiced. Flagged for the pedagogy class as a possible strengthen-the-fence candidate (e.g. have the screen-and-ready prompt self-report whether it paced or dumped, so the tell surfaces even on a clean run) — outside story's lane to prescribe.
